title: Integrity
body: Integrity is how whole the cell is. Three things wear it down, and they add together: hot water, a deep osmotic shrivel, and an empty ATP pool whose upkeep is still unpaid. A full dose of heat kills in about twenty seconds, a full shrivel in about thirty, and full starvation in about forty-five. The vitals line names which one is winning.

When the stress stops, the cell mends, all the way back from the brink in about a minute. If integrity reaches nothing, the body collapses and tears apart. A sister cell, if you have one, is still alive on her own stores.
